Because they don’t have that match experience, sometimes the girls are unable to handle certain situations in the middle. This is our shortcoming. Sri Lanka Cricket is trying to give the players more matches to overcome this situation,” he said.

The standout player in the Pakistan Women’s Under-19 T20 Tri-Series was left-handed opening batter Sanjana Kavindi, who won the Player of the Tournament award. 

“If you take the players from all the three teams, Sanjana is someone special. We always prepare her mindset – how she can stay at the crease for a longer period and play her natural game, rather than score quick runs and get out. We prepared her to carry the team and to finish the game and she did it,” said Peiris.

Apart from Kavindi, the other players who shone with the bat were Vimoksha Balasuriya, Nethmi Upeksha, Limansa Thilakarathna, and Umayangana Peiris, and among the bowlers skipper Chamudi Pramoda, Chamodhi Herath, Limansa Thilakarathna, Danodya Sewmini, and Nethmi Upeksha, who played her role well as a batting all-rounder.

Peiris, a talented left-hand batsman and prolific run scorer in the domestic circuit with over 6,600 first-class runs, was of the view that this present Under-19 side will be the future of Sri Lanka women’s cricket.

“In another two years’ time, these players will dominate Sri Lanka cricket. The way they are progressing, I am confident that we are in good space because we are improving our bench strength with these players. Three years ago, we didn’t have a bench for selection, but now with these players, there is going to be competition for places in the national women’s cricket team. They have watched how our national cricketers are performing and are improving their game. With the bench getting stronger, women’s cricket is also bound to improve immensely,” said Peiris, who is a High Performance Centre Coach for the past eight years and has also been involved with the national men’s team and coached several clubs and provincial sides.

title: Sri Lanka Sevens fight back to 5th as Soori bows out after 17 years | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 03:05
-     - 7

By Shamseer Jaleel at Racecourse

Srinath Sooriyabandara

SRI Lanka's men's sevens outfit, under skipper Janidu Dilshan, produced an encouraging comeback to finish fifth at the Asia Rugby Sevens Series 2026 second leg, which concluded at the Racecourse Grounds in Colombo yesterday.

The home side improved on their seventh-place finish at the opening leg in China, showing greater determination and composure in front of their home supporters. The tournament also marked an emotional milestone as veteran sevens star Srinath Sooriyabandara played his final game for Sri Lanka after a distinguished career spanning more than 17 years.

Sri Lanka made an encouraging start on day one, recording victories over the United Arab Emirates and India to finish second in their group behind Hong Kong China. However, their Cup quarter-final hopes ended when China edged them out 26–19 on day two.

The hosts bounced back strongly in the classification matches, defeating the UAE 26–10 in the fifth-place semi-final before producing an impressive 33–5 victory over Malaysia to secure fifth place overall. Sri Lanka ended the two-leg event in sixth place.

Hong Kong China dominated Malaysia 78–0 in the Cup quarter-finals before reaching the final with a 45–7 semi-final win over Thailand. Japan proved too strong for China in the other semi-final, winning 33–0.

Japan then completed a memorable double in Colombo, claiming both the men’s and women’s titles. The Japanese men defeated Hong Kong China 28–14 in the final, while their women’s team overcame China 14–7 to secure the second title. But on aggregate, Hong Kong China won the men’s series, while Japan won the women’s segment, overcoming China, who were placed second.

China claimed third place in the men’s competition with a 21–12 victory over Thailand.

Sri Lanka’s women also had a mixed campaign, beating Uzbekistan 19–15 before losing narrowly to Malaysia 10–5. They finished 10th in the 11-team competition. Overall, Sri Lanka’s women ended 11th in the 12-team event, with Iran, unable to find a flight to Colombo, finishing last in this segment.

Despite the disappointment of missing the Cup semi-finals, Sri Lanka’s improvement from seventh to fifth place offered encouragement. The occasion was particularly significant as Sooriyabandara brought the curtain down on a remarkable 17-year journey in Sri Lankan sevens rugby.

title: Haaland’s record scoring spree helps Man City to seventh Premier League win | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 03:00
-     - 4

Erling Haaland celebrates scoring Manchester City’s second goal in front of home fans holding up inflatable bananas during the Premier League match against Ipswich Town at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester on Saturday

The ongoing financial scandal enveloping Manchester City is not affecting the team’s results in the Premier League, nor has it diminished Erling Haaland’s appetite for goals.

Playing in front of fans waving inflatable bananas, City became only the third team to open a Premier League season with seven straight wins by beating Ipswich 3-2 at home on Saturday. Haaland netted twice to move to a season-high eight goals for a campaign being played under a cloud of controversy.

That made it back-to-back victories in the League for City, either side of a 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, since being found guilty of large-scale financial wrongdoing in the Premier League for nearly a decade. The seismic verdict threatens the club’s place in England’s lucrative top flight, though City continue to protest their innocence and have appealed.

City Manager Enzo Maresca believes the saga has galvanised the squad, and the defiance among the fanbase continued, with many supporters bringing along inflatable bananas – a throwback to an item that fans brought to games in the 1980s for fun amid tough times for the team – for Ipswich’s visit. They also jeered the Premier League anthem before kickoff.

“The fans, the club, the players – we are all together in this journey,” Maresca said of City’s defiance in troubled times.

“Going down with the City” was the chant by some home fans in the first half at the Etihad Stadium as they watched their team extend their lead in the league to six points.

Haaland and second-half substitute Antoine Semenyo were seen hobbling off the field at the end of the game, which finished with Ipswich grabbing its second goal in stoppage time and piling on the pressure in the final minutes.

The Norwegian has become the fastest player in Premier League history to score 100 non-penalty goals. It took him 139 matches to achieve this record.

Maresca said Haaland, who had taken a blow to the foot late in the match, was not worried.

Maresca also became the first Manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team.
